commands.command: deno eval <read-only PILOT-002 alternate-base identity probe>

evidence: Exact base-to-candidate lifecycle and Git validation paths showed no separate correctness finding beyond the contract and control failures.
The v1 grandfathering identity omits the authority-bearing base revision; see AUTONOMY-001-R1-SEC-002.
The canonical packet is rejected because authorization is compared with ordinary writes; see AUTONOMY-001-R1-ARCH-001.
Git subprocess consumption, output/path/blob limits, ancestry checks, and cleanup fixtures showed no material performance or resource finding.
The workflow changes are localized and readable with no independent maintainability finding.
The clean candidate passed 136 tests and exact 100 percent coverage, but omitted negative cases permit a trivial-success task definition; see AUTONOMY-001-R1-TDD-003.
RED, GREEN, and REFACTOR evidence showed no test weakening.

findings.expectedBehavior: Authorization paths exactly equal the protected .codex/.agents subset of allowedWrites; ordinary writes remain governed only by allowedWrites.
findings.observedBehavior: Authorization is compared with the complete allowedWrites array, so valid mixed protected and ordinary scope is rejected.
findings.reproduction: Run deno task ticket:validate docs/planning/tickets/AUTONOMY-001 and observe authorization_mismatch.
findings.impact: The accepted mixed-path maintenance workflow cannot pass canonical validation without misstating authority scope.
findings.requiredRemediation: Compare authorization with only the protected allowed-write subset and reject missing, extra, duplicate, or ordinary authorization entries.
findings.verification: Add mixed-scope positive and missing, extra, duplicate, and ordinary-entry negative regressions, then validate the canonical packet.

findings.expectedBehavior: Only exact content-addressed PILOT-001 and PILOT-002 v1 packet identities are grandfathered, including the exact base revision.
findings.observedBehavior: The digest replaces baseRevision with a sentinel, so an alternate authority anchor avoids legacy_packet_mismatch.
findings.reproduction: Replace PILOT-002 baseRevision and matching bundle references with existing commit 5cdf892a0669b25b447cf782e280530b66a6ed25; structural validation returns no issue.
findings.impact: A reused v1 identity can move its execution anchor while avoiding v2 authority and revision-bound controls.
findings.requiredRemediation: Hash the complete immutable canonical ticket identity, including baseRevision, and pin only accepted full identities.
findings.verification: Mutate baseRevision and every authority-bearing field of both legacy packets; every mutation must return legacy_packet_mismatch while exact packets remain valid.

findings.expectedBehavior: Trivially successful task definitions cannot serve as required ticket-wide gates even with an unchanged independent guard.
findings.observedBehavior: Only literal deno eval true is rejected; deno eval false exits zero and evades the no-op diagnostic.
findings.reproduction: Run deno eval false and observe exit 0; substitute it into the changed-task fixture and observe no task_definition_noop issue.
findings.impact: A changed required gate can become a trivial success while still being recorded and integrated as passing.
findings.requiredRemediation: Reject conservative eval-style trivial commands or positively allow only repository-approved executable gate forms.
findings.verification: Parameterize deno eval false, empty/string/numeric expressions, Deno.exit(0), and equivalent trivial-success forms; each must return task_definition_noop while legitimate guarded changes remain accepted.

notes: The round mismatch and null integrationRevision diagnostics are controller metadata staging issues, not candidate production findings.
